properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 21 at 4:10PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has
issued the following...

WHAT...Ozone Action Day Alert.

WHERE...Douglas, Jefferson, Denver, western Arapahoe, western
Adams, Broomfield, Boulder, Larimer, and Weld Counties

WHEN...400 PM Tuesday July 21 to 400 PM Wednesday July 22

IMPACTS...Ozone Action Day Alert is now in effect for the Front
Range Urban Corridor.  Hot and sunny weather with limited chances
for afternoon storms will allow ozone concentrations to reach the
Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups category on Tuesday and Wednesday.
On Tuesday elevated ozone is possible in the Denver Metro area,
Fort Collins, Greeley, and surrounding areas. On Wednesday the
highest ozone is expected to be confined to locations within the
Denver Metro area. For Colorado air quality conditions, forecasts,
and advisories, visit:
https://www.colorado.gov/airquality/colorado_summary.aspx   If
possible, please help us reduce ozone pollution by limiting
driving gas and diesel-powered vehicles until at least 4 p.m.
Wednesday, July 22, 2026. Colorado is also addressing ozone
pollution through state policies. For more information about
health impacts and how ozone pollution forms in Colorado, visit:
https://cdphe.colorado.gov/ozone- pollution-and-your-health

HEALTH INFORMATION...Increasing likelihood of respiratory symptoms
and breathing discomfort in active children and adults and people
with lung disease, such as asthma. Active children and adults, and
people with lung disease, such as asthma, should reduce prolonged
or heavy outdoor exertion.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.areaDesc: Kivalina and Red Dog Dock; Lower Kobuk Valley; Baldwin Peninsula; Northern Seward Peninsula
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 21 at 3:11PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Confidence is building in this storm taking a more southerly track
towards the Yukon Delta Wednesday evening, with model guidance
coalescing around the low reaching Norton Sound by late Wednesday
night/early Thursday morning. Fortunately, it doesn't appear to
be a storm that would come with major impacts. However, there is
a chance for minor coastal impacts and high surf due to gusty
southeast winds during the first half of the storm as it looks to
strengthen a bit before landfall, then west-northwest winds as
the low passes through. We will continue to update as necessary
throughout the week.

NWSheadline: Bering Sea Low Moving Ashore Wednesday Evening through Early Thursday Morning

properties.description:
AQAHGX

The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) has issued an
Ozone Action Day for the Houston, Galveston, and Brazoria area for
Wednesday, July 22, 2026.

Atmospheric conditions are expected to be favorable for producing
high levels of ozone pollution in the Houston, Galveston, and
surrounding areas on Wednesday. You can help prevent ozone pollution by
sharing a ride, walking, riding a bicycle, taking your lunch to work,
avoiding drive through lanes, conserving energy and keeping your vehicle
properly tuned.

For more information on ozone:

Ozone: The Facts www.tceq.texas.gov/airquality/monops/ozonefacts.html

EPA AirNow: www.airnow.gov/?city=Houston&state=TX&country=USA

properties.areaDesc: Benton, WA; Franklin, WA; Walla Walla, WA
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 20 at 7:40PM PDT by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
The Washington State Department of Ecology, Benton Clean Air Agency,
have issued an Air Quality Alert until 9 AM PDT Wednesday.

For the Smoke Air Quality Alert, wildfires burning in the region
combined with forecasted conditions will cause air quality to reach
unhealthy levels.

Pollutants in smoke can cause burning eyes, runny nose, aggravate
heart and lung diseases, and aggravate other serious health
problems.  Limit outdoor activities and keep children indoors if it
is smoky. Please follow medical advice if you have a heart or lung
condition.

Information from the Washington Department of Ecology web site is
available at http://www.ecy.wa.gov/air.html or call 360-407-6000.

Information from the Benton County Clean Air Agency web site is
available at http://www.bentoncleanair.org or call 509-783-1304.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

NWSheadline: AIR QUALITY ALERT IN EFFECT UNTIL 9 AM PDT WEDNESDAY
